fact: The Media Foundation for West Africa reports the Cybercrime Unit arrested opposition MPs Mariem Mint Cheikh on 9 April 2026 and Ghame Achour Salem on 10 April 2026 over social media videos criticising President Ghazouani, under Law No. 2021-021 on national symbols.

The Media Foundation for West Africa says journalist Warda Ahmed Souleymane was arrested on 31 October 2025 over a Facebook post calling for peaceful protest against the government and charged on 6 November 2025 with undermining state security.

The Media Foundation for West Africa reports Mauritanian authorities permanently shut down the news website Anbaa.info after its licence was revoked by the Ministry of Communication in July 2025 and its editor was summoned by the Cybercrime Unit on 25 August 2025 on a complaint from the regulator HAPA.

The Media Foundation for West Africa reports the news site Anbaa.info was closed for good in August 2025, after the Cybercrime Unit summoned its editor-in-chief, over analytical articles on Mauritania-Algeria relations published since 2022.
The Media Foundation for West Africa reports that in March 2024 the regulator HAPA sanctioned Anbaa.info for 'attacks against Algeria', making the site inaccessible for 60 days.
Le360 reports that mobile internet was cut in Mauritania during the 2025 exam period (23 June to 10 July), disrupting traders' mobile-money and online sales, according to traders it interviewed.

The #KeepItOn coalition states that after protests following the 29 June 2024 election, authorities disrupted mobile internet for 22 days from 2 July to 24 July 2024, shutting down Mattel and Chinguitel, which a government spokesperson reportedly justified as necessary for security.

AfriqueITNews reports a court on 4 May 2026 sentenced two opposition MPs, Mariem Cheikh Dieng and Ghamou Achour, to four years in prison for social media videos denouncing 'apartheid', and ordered their accounts closed; a lawyer was also arrested after a Facebook Live.

Government spokesman Nani Ould Chrouga defended the July 2024 internet cut as subject to legal procedures and a security necessity, and the digital minister said he hoped service would soon be restored.
CIPESA says Mauritania restricted mobile internet for 22 days from 2 July 2024 after the 29 June presidential election and protests disputing the result.
CIPESA says Mauritania cut mobile internet for nearly a week during protests in May and June 2023.
